Title: Delivery Engineer, ML, Americas
Description: About Hilbert Hilbert is a scalable, data science-first growth engine that gives B2C teams predictive clarity into user behavior, revenue drivers, and the actions that drive sustainable growth. Fully agentic by design, Hilbert shrinks months-long decision cycles to minutes. From Fortune 10 enterprises to beloved brands like FreshDirect, Blank Street, and Levain Bakery, operators run their growth on Hilbert. We're also co-building alongside leading AI companies. The Mission: Turn Ground Truth Into Growth Hilbert has two parts: a data foundation that gives our AI agents a high-fidelity view of each business, and an agentic web app where growth teams find and act on insights. The scores and audiences you build feed both: our agents reason with them, and our activation sends them into paid media and CRM. The hard problem Every customer's data is different, their compute may be ClickHouse, Databricks, Snowflake or BigQuery, and their teams want proof, not promises. Your models have to work in that environment and show measured uplift. We want every pod to stay lean and efficient across very different customer environments, delivering quality work at startup speed. You focus on delivery; our sales engineers handle pre-sales. Your work centers on customers in your own region: supporting customers elsewhere is a rare exception, and your global work is mainly staying aligned with Hilbert colleagues in other regions. What You'll Do Feature stores: build customer-specific, point-in-time correct features on the data foundation. Models: train, tune and validate propensity, churn, lifetime value, uplift and custom models, starting from our ML templates and building custom models when a customer needs something the templates don't cover. New model types that many customers will need are built first by our product engineering team, and you roll them out to later customers. Model analysis: go beyond aggregate metrics to verify what each model has learned, what drives its scores, and how it behaves across segments and on edge cases. Deployment: models run in the customer's own environment or on our managed stack. In either case, understand the constraints, pin down the requirements, design the ML system to fit, and write the scores and audiences our agents and activation use. Measurement: own the statistical design inside our growth team's measurement plan, from power and holdout setup to uplift analysis. Trust: document models for the customer's data science and risk teams, then monitor and retrain them in production. Productization: turn repeated features and model patterns into product with our product engineering team. What Success Looks Like Audiences built from your models lift the agreed growth metric, such as conversion or retention, against a holdout group, and that result decides whether the customer takes them to production. Who You Are The translator: you explain a model to a customer's data science team and earn their trust. The experimenter: you'd rather prove uplift in a holdout test than show off an offline metric. The pilot: you get the most out of AI agents across model iterations, from feature ideas and experiment runs to error analysis, and help build them into how the team works. The systems thinker: you build reusable features, pipelines and automation instead of one-off models, so a small team can deliver across very different environments. Extensive applied ML experience on tabular customer data, with strong Python and ML libraries. Extensive hands-on deep learning experience, from designing architectures and loss functions to training and shipping models in production, with PyTorch or a similar framework. Feature engineering in SQL warehouses such as Databricks, Snowflake or BigQuery. Working data engineering experience: building and debugging pipelines, data orchestration, data modeling and data quality checks, enough to own your feature pipelines end to end with our data engineers. Production ML with tools such as MLflow, Weights & Biases or Vertex AI. Solid experiment design and uplift measurement. Comfortable working in a distributed team across time zones. Fluent Spanish for roles based in Latin America. Nice to have DevOps, software architecture and security knowledge Growth-focused data projects experience Industry experience such as e-commerce, retail, fintech, telco and media Model governance in regulated industries such as banking and telco: model documentation, explainability and PII handling Able to travel to the US when necessary Reporting and location You report to your pod's Lead Delivery Engineer and work alongside our data delivery engineers and product engineering team. The role is based in Americas. Delivery runs remotely, with occasional visits to our largest customers. Why join us At Hilbert, we move fast, work collaboratively, and give people real ownership over their impact. As a fast-growing company, there's no shortage of room to grow — you'll take on new challenges quickly and shape the path as you go. Hilbert is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive culture, and we welcome applicants of all backgrounds. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

Title: Lead Product Data Analyst
Description: About LawnStarter LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings and two consecutive years of profitability. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services, and we're investing in the next generation of our platform to get there. About The Team We're a high-leverage team of Product Data Analysts embedded across the business, owning the semantic layer and the metrics everyone trusts. We turn "I have a hunch" into "here's what actually happened," and we're the reason teams across the company can make calls on evidence instead of instinct. This role brings dedicated analytical firepower to the Pro (supply) side of that work. Requirements The Role As a Lead Product Data Analyst, you'll directly impact our results through insights and reports. You'll work closely with product managers, researchers, and other business stakeholders, helping with prioritization, assessments, and business recommendations. Alongside the rest of the Analytics team, it's your responsibility to nurture the data-driven culture within the company, making data easier to consume, whether through interactive reports, easy-to-use datasets, documentation, or training. You'll work with the autonomy of a Lead: setting your own standards, working independently, and acting as a trusted thought partner rather than an order-taker. That title isn't about managing people, there's no team attached to it. It's about the bar you hold your own analysis to, and the bar you help everyone around you reach. This role leans toward the Pro (supply) side of our marketplace, though the exact focus flexes with where the business needs the most insight. What You'll Own Modeling & Analysis: A marketplace is a complex system, with many moving parts and often contradicting signals. That creates an exciting pool of opportunities to find gaps, insights, and optimizations. Analyses range from a simple A/B test to a multivariate model on retention or ETA, backed by advanced SQL and intermediate Python or R Reporting: A complex system produces a high number of metrics worth tracking. A dashboard is only as good as our trust that it's correct and current. You'll understand the needs of the teams you work with and help create and maintain the reporting system, keeping it organized and easy to act on Analytics Engineering: Occasionally you'll work in the inner layers of the Data Warehouse to provide clean, documented datasets that power our reports and end users. We use dbt for transformation, so SQL is a must Problems to Solve Metrics nobody fully trusts. Different teams cite different numbers for the same thing, and no one's quite sure which is current. Untangling that and giving the business one number it can stand behind is core to the job. Analysis that ships but doesn't move anything. A technically correct answer that doesn't change a single decision is still a failure. Getting a stakeholder to actually act on what you found is the hard part, not the SQL. Data that's hard for anyone but an analyst to touch. If every question requires filing a ticket and waiting on you, you haven't built a data-driven culture, you've built a bottleneck. A system with too many moving parts and not enough signal. Supply, demand, pricing, and service quality all interact. Teasing out what's actually driving a metric versus what's noise is a real analytical problem, not a formality. What Success Looks Like (Year 1) The metrics teams rely on daily are trusted, documented, and current, no one's quietly keeping a shadow spreadsheet because they don't trust the dashboard Routine questions are self-serve: stakeholders find their own answers in existing reports instead of pinging you for a one-off pull You can name specific decisions your analysis changed, not just analyses you delivered The datasets and models you've built in dbt are clean and documented enough that other analysts build on them without redoing your work Who You Are AI-Native: You use AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and similar) daily to move faster: drafting and debugging SQL and dbt models, scripting analysis, and shaping reports, and you keep experimenting with new capabilities as they show up. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI tools or prefer to do everything by hand. Learning Mindset: You take pride in understanding problems deeply and asking the right questions before reaching for an answer. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you have a preconceived system of processes and methods and plan on just applying them without first learning all the ways our business is unique. Sets the Bar: As a Lead, you work autonomously, hold your own analysis to a high standard, and raise the bar for the people around you, whether or not they report to you. Product managers and stakeholders should see you as a trusted thought partner, not an order-taker. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you want a title and a team before you're willing to raise everyone else's standards. Team Player: You are ready to work alongside exceptional people, helping them achieve great results. You create an environment where people are excited to work with you daily, with intellectual honesty and trust. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you value being right over reaching the right answer together. Business Focus: You care deeply about understanding business needs and how your analysis connects with our product, customers, and financials. You can envision how metrics drill down from the highest to the lowest level, identifying what needs to be analyzed or reported on at each. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're happiest doing analysis for its own sake, disconnected from a decision it will drive. Bias for Action: You understand that despite your careful approach to understanding problems, you actively avoid being a perfectionist or getting tied up in knots. You have a bias for action to make progress, and you enjoy being scrappy, with constraints that enthrall you. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you, by default, like building full solutions from the get-go. This Role Is NOT A ticket queue. You're not here to pull numbers on demand, you decide what's worth measuring and how to measure it A dashboard-admin seat. Maintaining BI tooling is part of the job, not the point of it. The point is the insight the dashboard delivers A people-management role. This is an individual-contributor seat. "Lead" describes the bar you hold yourself and others to, not a team you manage A role that waits for perfectly clean data. If you need data handed to you pre-cleaned before you can start, this isn't the right seat, you're expected to get your hands into the warehouse Tools of the Trade SQL and dbt for transformation and modeling, Python or R for the occasional statistical deep dive, and Lightdash as our primary BI layer for dashboards and self-serve reporting. Benefits Base salary: $75,000-$100,000 USD annually AI tooling provided: The Claude routines already running pieces of our experimentation process are yours to extend, not a side project you have to justify Fully remote: This is deep-focus analytical work with US-facing partners. We hire the best analyst regardless of city and trust you to manage your environment and overlap hours Flexible PTO: Measured on outcomes, not hours logged VERY IMPORTANT REMINDER: Please upload your English resume. Applications without it will not be considered.

Monitor the adoption and commercial influence of insights, gathering feedback and applying learning to future work. What We’re Looking For 4+ years of relevant experience in insights, analytics, market research, consumer research, marketing strategy or a related analytical discipline. Minimum of 2 years of regular experience querying and manipulating data using SQL. Demonstrated experience using data to solve commercial or marketing challenges and influence stakeholder decisions. Strong insight storytelling skills, with the ability to turn complex evidence into clear recommendations for different professional audiences. Experience building high-quality presentations in Google Slides, PowerPoint or an equivalent tool. Confidence presenting analytical work to clients, agencies or senior internal stakeholders. Ability to clarify ambiguous requests, manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work independently. Working knowledge of quantitative and qualitative research methods, audience research, market intelligence or syndicated data. Title: Delivery Engineer, Data, Americas
Description: About Hilbert Hilbert is a scalable, data science-first growth engine that gives B2C teams predictive clarity into user behavior, revenue drivers, and the actions that drive sustainable growth. Fully agentic by design, Hilbert shrinks months-long decision cycles to minutes. From Fortune 10 enterprises to beloved brands like FreshDirect, Blank Street, and Levain Bakery, operators run their growth on Hilbert. We're also co-building alongside leading AI companies. The Mission: Turn Ground Truth Into Growth Hilbert has two parts: a data foundation that gives our AI agents a high-fidelity view of each business, and an agentic web app where growth teams find and act on insights. The scores and audiences you build feed both: our agents reason with them, and our activation sends them into paid media and CRM. The hard problem The challenge isn't moving rows; it's reasoning consistency. Our AI must produce the same high-quality insights wherever the data lives, from data that is different at every customer. We want every pod to stay lean and efficient across very different customer environments, delivering quality work at startup speed. You focus on delivery; our sales engineers handle pre-sales. Your work centers on customers in your own region: supporting customers elsewhere is a rare exception, and your global work is mainly staying aligned with Hilbert colleagues in other regions. What You'll Do Data discovery: work with the customer's engineers to understand their sources, and help build our Data Discovery Agent, which will analyze data, suggest mappings and scaffold first pipelines. Canonical modeling: map source data into Hilbert's unified growth models, and help shape new models for industries we haven't served yet. Hybrid integration: build and run ETL and ELT pipelines through Hilbert's data orchestration layer, which controls them whether they run on our stack (Dagster, Airbyte, ClickHouse) or natively in the customer's warehouse. AI semantic layer: define the metadata, metrics and business logic in our semantic layer, built on Cube (cube.dev), that let our agents understand custom data without hallucinating. Secure integration: connect Hilbert and the customer's cloud with least-privilege access and private connectivity. Data quality: own monitoring and quality checks until the deployment is production-ready, and keep it healthy. Productization: turn repeated work into product with our product engineering team. Who You Are The translator: you earn the trust of a customer's data architect quickly and turn the logic of their custom tables into something our reasoning engine understands. The data ontologist: you know AI needs more than a table; it needs context, and you have the discipline to define what the data means. The pilot: you're excited to help build AI agents that take on the heavy lifting of discovery and pipeline scaffolding. The systems thinker: you build reusable patterns, tests and automation instead of one-off pipelines, so a small team can deliver across very different environments without cutting corners. The adapter: you're at home in whatever environment a customer brings, from their cloud and warehouse to their security rules, and you find a working solution quickly. Extensive data engineering experience, with expert SQL and data modeling, strong Python, and dbt or Spark. Hands-on with Databricks, Snowflake (including Snowpark) or BigQuery, and ClickHouse, plus an orchestrator such as Dagster or Airflow. Working knowledge of cloud IAM and networking on AWS, Azure or GCP. Comfortable working in a distributed team across time zones. Fluent Spanish for roles based in Latin America. Nice to have ML engineering experience DevOps, software architecture and security knowledge Growth-focused data projects experience Industry experience such as e-commerce, retail, fintech, telco and media Able to travel to the US when necessary Why join us At Hilbert, we move fast, work collaboratively, and give people real ownership over their impact. We’re a small, fully remote team that moves quickly and ships real things. About the Role We’re looking for a hands-on Growth Marketing Engineer to own our full-funnel demand engine and turn the traffic and buying signals we already generate into qualified demos and pipeline. You’ll sit at the intersection of performance marketing, marketing operations, conversion optimization, and analytics, building and running the systems that move a prospect from first touch to booked meeting. This is a builder’s role: you’ll spend your days in the ad platforms, the CRM, the analytics tools, and the page builder, shipping changes and measuring their impact on qualified-demo volume and pipeline. What You’ll Do Paid acquisition: Plan, launch, and optimize paid campaigns (Google Ads — Performance Max and Search, LinkedIn), architecting campaign structure, audience targeting, and conversion-event mapping so spend optimizes toward booked demos and pipeline rather than clicks, with clean, server-imported conversion tracking (enhanced/offline conversions from the CRM). Conversion rate optimization: Build and A/B test dedicated demo landing pages, landing pages, forms, and CTAs that turn visitors into meetings, including persona-aware routing (buyer vs. candidate vs. partner) across the site, and own the on-site demo path. Marketing operations & RevOps: Own the full lead lifecycle and the automation behind it — CRM workflows, lifecycle-stage instrumentation, lead scoring and routing, and the visitor-signal-to-outbound engine across HubSpot, Amplemarket, RB2B, Duo, and Zapier. Build and scale the loop that turns identified in-market website visitors into timely, signal-based 1:1 outreach. Email deliverability & infrastructure: Own outbound sending infrastructure — mailbox and domain strategy, warm-up and rotation, pre-send verification, and deliverability health — so outreach lands in the inbox and protects the primary domain’s reputation. Analytics & reporting : Build and own the measurement layer end to end — define the key conversion events, GA4, UTM governance, conversion validation — and build the dashboards that tie marketing activity to pipeline and revenue (Mode). Conversion copywriting: Write the ad, landing-page, and signal-based outbound copy that drives response. What You’ll Need Hands-on experience across growth marketing, demand generation, marketing operations, or revenue operations — ideally in B2B SaaS. You’re a builder who works inside the tools, not only a strategist. Real performance-marketing experience, especially Google Ads (including Performance Max and Search campaign structure), with a habit of optimizing toward CAC and pipeline instead of vanity metrics. Fluency with a modern marketing / CRM automation stack (we use HubSpot, Amplemarket, RB2B, Intercom, Zapier, and Calendly; comparable tools like Salesforce, Marketo, or Make are fine). Analytics chops: GA4, disciplined UTM and conversion tracking, and enough SQL / BI to build your own dashboards (we use Mode; Looker, Amplitude, or similar is fine). CRO instincts and conversion copywriting ability. A data-driven, experimental, self-directed way of working — you read the funnel, ship the fix, and measure the result. Bilingual Spanish/English, with fluent written English. This is our ideal profile, not a checklist. If you can do the work, we’d love to hear from you regardless of years or title. Success Metrics (First 6–12 Months) Growth in qualified demos and marketing-sourced pipeline, at flat or lower cost per acquisition. Higher conversion rates across the funnel, from visitor to demo to booked meeting. A larger share of best-fit (ICP) traffic reached and converted. Strong outbound deliverability and healthy sending infrastructure across all domains. A reliable weekly reporting cadence that ties marketing activity to pipeline. Nice to Have Experience in HR tech, workforce, background screening, or compliance-adjacent categories. Account-based marketing (ABM) and audience segmentation. Server-side, enhanced, or offline conversion tracking (e.g. CAPI). Outbound email deliverability at scale — multi-domain/mailbox management, warm-up, and inbox placement. Technical SEO and simple creative for ads and social. Perks & Compensation Competitive salary (base range shared early in the process) Major medical health insurance Paid time off Remote work with occasional in-office training and in-person meetings

Title: Data Engineer, Amazon Music

Title: Lead AI Product Engineer
Description: ¿Buscas generar impacto en una empresa transnacional líder con tus conocimientos? ¡Esta oportunidad te está esperando! Aon está en el negocio de tomar las mejores decisiones. En Aon, tomamos mejores decisiones para proteger y enriquecer la vida de las personas alrededor del mundo. Como organización, estamos unidos a través de la confianza y nos apasiona ayudar a nuestros colegas y clientes a alcanzar el éxito. ¿Cómo será un día típico? El Lead AI Product Engineer será responsable de desarrollar e integrar capacidades de Inteligencia Artificial dentro de las soluciones digitales de Aon, traduciendo las necesidades del negocio en funcionalidades útiles, confiables y fáciles de mantener. La posición será el referente técnico para los componentes de IA asignados , participando desde la experimentación y el desarrollo hasta su implementación en producción y mejora continua, en colaboración con los equipos de Arquitectura, Desarrollo y otras áreas de Tecnología. Es una posición principalmente hands-on , con autonomía y responsabilidad técnica sobre los componentes de IA dentro de las soluciones asignadas. El nivel Lead refleja la responsabilidad de guiar decisiones de implementación, asegurar la calidad de las entregas y mantener continuidad técnica durante todo el ciclo de vida. Inicialmente, la posición no tendrá reportes directos. Principales responsabilidades Diseñar, desarrollar e integrar componentes de Inteligencia Artificial dentro de la arquitectura establecida para cada solución. Implementar capacidades utilizando Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), embeddings, agentes y herramientas de orquestación, cuando el caso de uso lo justifique. Conectar componentes de IA con APIs, aplicaciones y fuentes de información aprobadas. Desarrollar prototipos y evolucionarlos hacia implementaciones mantenibles, evitando complejidad innecesaria. Actuar como referente técnico para los componentes de IA dentro del alcance de la posición. Proponer alternativas de implementación y explicar sus beneficios, limitaciones, costos y dependencias. Definir y ejecutar pruebas para validar la calidad de los resultados, comportamiento del sistema, desempeño y manejo de errores. Implementar controles de seguridad, trazabilidad y monitoreo acordados con los equipos correspondientes. Documentar y mantener código, prompts, configuraciones y decisiones técnicas. Trabajar con Arquitectura y stakeholders del negocio para traducir necesidades en funcionalidades y criterios de aceptación. Proporcionar estimaciones técnicas e identificar riesgos y dependencias. Revisar entregables relacionados con IA desarrollados por proveedores o equipos internos. Apoyar en la implementación en producción y solución de problemas de los componentes desarrollados. Incorporar retroalimentación de usuarios y resultados de uso para mejorar continuamente las funcionalidades. Habilidades y experiencia que te llevarán al éxito Licenciatura o Ingeniería en Software, Ciencias de la Computación, Sistemas de Información o alguna disciplina relacionada, o experiencia profesional equivalente. Sólidas bases de ingeniería de software, particularmente en desarrollo backend, APIs e integración de sistemas. Experiencia práctica desarrollando soluciones con modelos de lenguaje, más allá del uso de herramientas de IA conversacional. Conocimiento de LLMs, embeddings, recuperación de información, RAG, agentes y orquestación, así como criterio técnico para determinar cuándo utilizarlos. Dominio de Python u otro lenguaje relevante para la implementación de soluciones de IA. Experiencia con Git, code reviews, testing y documentación técnica. Capacidad para explicar decisiones técnicas, reconocer limitaciones y trabajar dentro de estándares y restricciones empresariales. Capacidad para demostrar una implementación concreta de IA y explicar el problema que resolvió, las decisiones tomadas, las pruebas realizadas y los aprendizajes obtenidos. Experiencia deseable Implementación de capacidades de IA en ambientes productivos. Experiencia trabajando con frameworks de agentes u orquestación. Familiaridad con servicios de cloud, deployment y observabilidad. Experiencia evaluando resultados generados por IA, monitoreando consumo y optimizando costos. Integración de IA con herramientas de automatización. Colaboración con proveedores de tecnología. No es necesario contar con dominio de todos los frameworks, experiencia entrenando foundation models o conocimientos avanzados de administración de infraestructura. ¿Cómo apoyamos a nuestros colegas? Asimismo, todos nuestros colegas disfrutan de dos “Global Wellbeing Days” al año, que les permiten dedicar tiempo a enfocarse en sí mismos. Ofrecemos diversas soluciones de trabajo flexible y reconocemos que la flexibilidad va más allá del lugar de trabajo. A esto lo llamamos Smart Working . Nuestra cultura de aprendizaje continuo te inspira y brinda las herramientas necesarias para aprender, compartir y desarrollarte, ayudándote a alcanzar tu máximo potencial. Como resultado, en Aon estarás más conectado, serás más relevante y tu contribución será valorada. Aon promueve un entorno de trabajo innovador donde todos nuestros colegas pueden ser ellos mismos. Aon brinda igualdad de oportunidades de empleo a todos los empleados y candidatos, sin distinción por características o condiciones protegidas por la legislación aplicable. Title: Director, Commercial Operations
Description: Overview About the Role & Team IDC is seeking a Director, Commercial Operations to provide senior-level insight and operating leadership across some of our most important commercial priorities. This person will have a broad view across the Commercial portfolio and work directly with senior leaders to understand performance, identify where we need to go deeper, and shape the decisions and actions that follow. They will not simply respond to questions or report results. We expect them to recognize the questions we should be asking, develop a point of view grounded in the data and business context, and bring forward clear recommendations. Much of the work will cross functions and organizational boundaries. The Director will bring senior leaders and teams together around complex issues, challenge assumptions when needed, create clarity around what needs to happen next, and help drive action on priorities that matter to the business. What You’ll Do Commercial Performance & Portfolio Analysis Own analysis of key Commercial KPIs, trends, variances, and performance drivers across the portfolio. Develop an integrated view across regions, segments, teams, and strategic priorities to identify where performance is changing, where risk is emerging, and where deeper attention is warranted. Bring together data from multiple sources, reconcile inconsistencies, and investigate results that do not immediately make sense. Look beyond headline numbers to understand underlying drivers, patterns, risks, and opportunities. Connect signals across different parts of the business to identify broader implications that may not be visible when each area is viewed independently. Strategic Insights & Decision Support Turn complex data and operational information into clear insights, implications, and recommended actions for senior leadership. Take broad or ambiguous commercial questions, determine what needs to be understood, and structure the analysis required to get there. Develop a point of view grounded in evidence and challenge assumptions when the data points somewhere else. Advise leadership on critical commercial priorities by clarifying what is working, what is not, what has changed, and what decisions or trade-offs may be required. Create executive reporting, business reviews, analyses, and presentations that make important issues easier to understand and act on. Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence Partner with senior leaders and teams across Commercial, Revenue Operations, Finance, Marketing, IT, and other functions on priorities that span organizational boundaries. Bring together the right information, perspectives, and expertise to create a shared understanding of complex issues. Build strong working relationships across departments and work through conflicting information, unclear ownership, or different points of view. Create clarity around the inputs, decisions, actions, and deliverables needed from each contributor. Hold owners accountable for commitments and follow through when required information, decisions, or actions are missing. Surface unresolved issues early and bring the right leaders together when progress requires broader coordination or intervention. Turning Insight Into Action Work with senior leaders and business owners to translate findings into clear actions and expected outcomes. Evaluate whether actions taken are actually changing the result and identify when a different response is needed. Recognize when an issue requires deeper analysis, a different approach, or senior leadership attention. Help leadership focus on the issues that matter most and make sure important findings do not stop at the report, dashboard, or presentation. Reporting & Process Improvement Continuously improve the reporting, metrics, dashboards, and analytical approaches used to understand Commercial performance and strategic priorities. Identify reporting and operational processes that are manual, fragmented, inconsistent, or harder than they need to be. Work with partner teams to improve data quality, standardization, automation, and recurring workflows. Build practical, scalable tools and processes that give leadership better visibility into the business and make it easier to identify issues and act on them. What Success Looks Like We are looking for someone who is analytical, commercially minded, and naturally curious. When something changes, they want to understand why. When the numbers do not add up, they keep digging until they do. They also need the judgment and credibility to operate with senior leaders across functions. This person should be comfortable with challenging assumptions, pushing for clarity, holding others accountable, and forming a point of view even when the answer is not obvious. Above all, we want someone senior leadership can trust to understand the business, identify what matters, and help shape the actions we take on our most important commercial priorities. What You Bring 8–12+ years of experience in Commercial Operations, Business Operations, Revenue Operations, Strategy, Transformation, Analytics, or a related field. Strong analytical skills and experience working with business performance data, KPIs, trends, and operational metrics. Demonstrated ability to move from data to insight, understand broader business implications, and develop clear recommendations. Experience advising senior leaders on high-priority business questions, strategic initiatives, or performance issues. Experience developing executive reporting, business reviews, analyses, and presentations for senior leadership. Strong ability to structure ambiguous questions, develop hypotheses, and work through complex problems independently. Advanced Excel skills and comfort working with large or complex data sets. Strong PowerPoint skills and the ability to turn detailed information into clear, concise executive communication. Demonstrated ability to partner with and influence senior stakeholders across multiple functions without direct authority. Experience improving reporting, workflows, or operating processes through better design, standardization, tools, or automation. Familiarity with Salesforce and business intelligence or reporting platforms is preferred. Strong communication, judgment, organization, and follow-through. Ability to navigate ambiguity, manage competing priorities, and operate with a high degree of independence. Why This Role Stands Out At IDC, your work helps shape how the world understands technology and where it goes next. You collaborate with curious, high-caliber colleagues who value rigor, integrity, and shared success. As the premier global provider of trusted technology intelligence, IDC equips business and technology leaders with the evidence they need to make confident decisions. Our insights inform strategy, investment, and innovation across industries and regions. Recognized by IIAR as Analyst Firm of the Year for five consecutive years, IDC sets the standard for credibility and impact. With more than 1,000 analysts worldwide and a truly global perspective, we combine deep expertise with practical relevance. Here, your ideas matter, your voice is heard, and your contributions provide the insights leaders rely on every day. It is meaningful work, backed by a culture that supports growth, collaboration, and long-term career development with a globally respected brand. Equal Opportunity Employer IDC is committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all qualified persons. Employment eligibility verification required. We participate in E-Verify. If this role relocates to a different country, the salary range will be updated to reflect that country's range, rather than a currency conversion of the original range.
